item: the Law and Press lanes' host counts are measured with a sweep that reads flow-style and native-script domain rows: Law 260 became 309, Press 9,033 became 9,035
summary: Follow-on to C-L2 (#1717), which found the gap. The scheme-less sweep behind every class lane's host count (_YAML_DOMAIN) missed two kinds of declared domain. (1) It read the block spelling of a row (domain: x on its own line) and none of the flow spelling (- {name: ..., domain: x, ...}), and configs/legal_sources.yml writes all 51 of its curated source rows in the flow spelling: 49 hosts the app seeds and crawls (wipolex.wipo.int, legifrance.gouv.fr, boe.es, congress.gov, govinfo.gov, sec.gov and 43 more; two of the 51 were already counted through a url) were absent from the Law lane's hostCount and from the SECURITY.md row, so the consent hover said 260 where the catalogues carry 309. (2) It read ASCII only, and configs/sources.yml declares three domains in their native script (the reviewer found them): the app reaches https://<domain> and requests sends the IDNA spelling, so xn--a-1fa.no (from the domain with an a-ring) and xn--ob0b790c.net (a Korean .net domain, reached elsewhere only as www.) were hosts the app can reach and the Press lane did not count; the third is the Russian domain whose punycode form a url already counted. Press 9,033 became 9,035. No host was added: the app could always reach them, the document did not say so. The regex reads both spellings and Unicode values (a key that merely ends in domain stays out; HONEST LIMIT: a {domain: x} inside a comment or a quoted string would match, none does today and two tests fail by name if one ever does), _ascii_host turns a native-script name into the one a connection uses, and hostCount and the **309** and **9,035** rows in docs/SECURITY.md move in the same diff (Q1001). The count guard could not have caught either miss because it measures with the regex it checks; a new test parses the same catalogues with a YAML reader (no shape filter, so a declared domain the shape check cannot read is named instead of dropped) and compares the domain sets both ways, a table pins block, indented, quoted, flow, tight, native-script rows and four non-matches, and a test writes small files to prove the comparison itself fails on a spelling the regex cannot read and on a domain the shape check drops. Mutants (9): old regex, ASCII-only value class, hostCount left stale, no normalisation in the count, identity _ascii_host, unreadable check removed, oracle re-filtered by shape, misses ignored, unanchored regex; all killed (the first version of the oracle test let an oracle-side shape filter survive, which is why the comparison is now a function with its own test). No schema change, no new host, no locale string.
